name: dbt Job Medallion Patterns in Fabric
description: Choose where dbt fits in a Fabric medallion (Bronze/Silver/Gold) architecture and orchestrate it. Covers the four documented patterns (Warehouse-only, Lakehouse landing + Warehouse transform, Lakehouse refine + Warehouse serve, Lakehouse-only) and the separate decision of native dbt scheduling vs orchestration inside a Fabric data pipeline. Uses fabio data-build-tool-job to create/run the dbt job and optionally data-pipeline to orchestrate it.
prerequisites: A Warehouse and/or Lakehouse for the medallion layers (fabio warehouse create / fabio lakehouse create)
A dbt project (the dbt job's definition) — data-build-tool-job is preview

steps.command: fabio warehouse create --workspace $WS --name analytics_dw    # and/or: fabio lakehouse create --workspace $WS --name raw_lh
steps.description: Provision the medallion targets. The pattern decides which engine owns which layer.
steps.notes: Pattern A Warehouse-only: Bronze+Silver+Gold in the Warehouse (SQL-first teams). Pattern B Lakehouse landing + Warehouse transform: land raw in a Lakehouse (OneLake), transform/serve in the Warehouse. Pattern C Lakehouse refine + Warehouse serve: engineering owns Lakehouse (Bronze/Silver), BI owns Warehouse (Gold) — distinct ownership boundaries. Pattern D Lakehouse-only: all layers in the Lakehouse with Spark execution (Delta-first).

steps.command: fabio data-build-tool-job create --workspace $WS --name dbt_transform --description "dbt Silver/Gold models"
steps.description: Create the dbt job item that owns transformation logic, testing, dependencies, and materialization.
steps.notes: dbt owns the transformation contract regardless of pattern; the pattern only changes which engine its models target (Warehouse T-SQL vs Lakehouse Spark).

steps.description: Upload the dbt project definition (models, profiles, sources).
steps.notes: Point dbt's target at the layer(s) it should own — a common split is dbt owning Silver+Gold while ingestion (COPY INTO / pipeline / Spark) owns Bronze.

steps.description: Native scheduling path: run the dbt job on-demand (or on its own schedule) and wait for completion.
steps.notes: Use this when dbt orchestration is sufficient — dbt manages model dependencies internally.

steps.command: fabio data-pipeline create --workspace $WS --name medallion_orchestration    # then add a dbt-job activity + upstream ingestion/downstream refresh
steps.description: Pipeline orchestration path (separate decision): wrap the dbt job in a Fabric data pipeline when you need end-to-end workflow dependencies (ingest Bronze -> run dbt Silver/Gold -> refresh a semantic model).
steps.notes: Architecture (where data/transforms live) and orchestration (native dbt vs pipeline) are INDEPENDENT choices — pick the engine per layer first, then choose how to run it.

steps.command: fabio data-build-tool-job run --workspace $WS --id $DBT_ID --wait --query 'status'    # or fabio job-scheduler get-instance --follow
steps.description: Verify the run outcome and monitor to completion.
steps.notes: Pair with the CI/CD deploy workflow to promote the dbt job + its targets between environments.

tips: There is no single right pattern — it depends on where data lands, which engine transforms it, and how curated data is consumed.
Keep dbt as the owner of transformation logic/testing/materialization in every pattern; change only the target engine.
Architecture vs orchestration are separate: choose the layer engines first, then native dbt scheduling vs a Fabric pipeline.
For SQL-first teams, Warehouse-only (Pattern A) minimizes engines; for Delta-first/Spark teams, Lakehouse-only (Pattern D) does.
See also: fabio context best-practices (deploy-parameters) to promote dbt jobs across environments, and the e2e medallion guidance.
